notes: Dev ABox contraction on a functional relation, paired with the revision history-replace-d001 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): it removes that revision's original fact, 'Louis XVI of France was married to Marie Antoinette' (same subject, relation spouse_of and old object), so revision and contraction can be compared directly. It replaces the earlier version, which removed 'The capital of West Germany was Bonn' (the pairing rule was added to the README on 2026-11-11). spouse_of is tagged symmetric and functional (one spouse at a time) in RELATIONS.md. Cardinality question: another candidate value, Archduchess Maria Elisabeth of Austria, Marie Antoinette's elder sister, 'no' before because Louis XVI had one wife; after the removal the reason for 'no' is gone, so 'does not know'. The first candidate, Olympe de Gouges, was dropped after review: she is known as Louis Aubry's widow, a commoner and a playwright, and a king's wife was queen by definition, so 'no' had strong routes that do not go through the removed marriage and a clean contraction could still answer 'no'. Maria Elisabeth fits the 'plausible match of his time' pattern of the geography template (Los Angeles for the capital of the United States): her sister's marriage to the Dauphin Louis Auguste was negotiated in 1768, the year she herself was proposed to his grandfather Louis XV (Wikipedia, 'Marriage negotiations'), and no text ties her to Louis XVI as a bride. Residual risk, recorded: her article says the plans of marriage fell through and describes her as unmarried like her sister Maria Anna, and she was an abbess in Innsbruck, so a model that holds that could answer 'no' by a route that skips the removed fact; it is far rarer than the routes of the first candidate, and a 'no' after editing is a kept route as well as a failed removal. The question is asked about 'married to', not 'could have been', to match the geography template; the cardinality question carries no derivability, as the validator requires. Relation note: spouse_of is tagged functional in RELATIONS.md but its reading is 'one spouse at a time' (replace d001's notes say so), so the tag is time-indexed; it behaves as functional here because Louis XVI married once and never remarried, which is why this subject is a fair test of the functional case. Both answers are stored: keeping the marriage from her side or under the description while dropping it from his is not a consistent contraction, so both are determinate.
